items.english: Getting the words across wrong like that, against his own intention, was one of his habits.
"What I think doesn't count, does it, or else as usual we'll end up not going."
"Not this time, surely —. You do the thinking. I don't know anywhere, so anywhere is bound to feel new and amusing. We might as well go meaning to settle."
notes: Kept the soft evasiveness: proposal left to her, commitment to nothing.

items.english: "Talk of settling sounds oppressive. Anyway, we'll have to find a rented house, some time. Tokyo again?"
"Mother says she doesn't mind joining us any time, but if you come there there'll be no study, will there?"
"As for having no study, I've got used to that from my Tokyo life till now."

Talking this over as they came round into the garden, they found two workmen settled on the veranda, stripped bare with their headbands knotted to the front. Wiping sweat and drinking tea, the two were lamenting that the carp simply could not be caught. Looking down at the reddish brown water, A folded his arms: "It clouds straight up like this—"
notes: Workmen for 鳢職, bare with headbands for 向う鉞巻の裸体; reddish brown for 赧土色. Dialect normalized to rough plain speech without borrowed dialect.

items.english: "It's no use, they're thoroughly shy now. The moment we put one foot in, they start thrashing first and cloud it all up!" B said, frowning.
notes: Kept catch and cloud in plain words for the repeated mechanism.

items.english: "At this rate it won't clear back to what it was till the day after tomorrow or so."
notes: Left unattributed as in Japanese; speaker floats between A and B.

items.english: "Shall we just go at them blind, one more push!"
"Once it's like this, aim or nothing, there's nothing to go by."

data.say: Drafted p33 to p44, keeping Taki evasive and the workmen rough with floating speakers.
